name: Inside python-coder (the coder's internal workflow)
summary: The internal workflow python-coder runs when the build pipeline's code step hands it a red baseline: it loads the project conventions / PROJECT_CONTEXT, edits only the ticket's files_touched to satisfy the red baseline, runs doc-enforcer on the changed Python, runs complexity-reduction, runs the suite until it is green, and finally records its sign-off via the signoff skill. This is the agent-altitude drill-down beneath the code step of how-a-ticket-is-built.

steps.label: Load conventions
steps.human: python-coder loads the project conventions / PROJECT_CONTEXT so it writes code that matches the repo's error-handling, style, and structure rules.

steps.label: Implement against red
steps.human: python-coder edits only the ticket's files_touched to satisfy the red baseline handed over by test-writer.

steps.label: Doc-enforcer
steps.human: doc-enforcer runs over the changed .py files to enforce docstring and documentation conventions.

steps.label: Complexity reduction
steps.human: python-coder runs complexity-reduction to keep the new code within the repo's complexity budget.

steps.label: Run until green
steps.human: test-runner runs the suite until every red_baseline test passes.

steps.label: Record sign-off
steps.human: python-coder records the sign-off via the signoff skill, updating the ticket frontmatter and the Sign-offs checklist together.

acceptance_scenarios.given: a red baseline handed over from test-writer
acceptance_scenarios.then: only files_touched are edited and the red_baseline tests are the target of the change
the coder does not sign off until every red_baseline test is green

provenance.note: Gold agent-internal flow; the drill-down target of the how-acs-are-built code step.
